text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — runtime queueing spike in us-east (95th latency + errors). Auto-pager fired for maya. Investigating source: sustained long-gen requests from multiple tenants. https://incident.redwood/INC-20260317 :rotating_light:

maya: On it. Seeing a burst of long-lived requests hitting model-mu routes. Initial triage: most tail time in decode stage. Prioritizing live mitigations — will coordinate throttles and shedding.

ajay: Don't nuke global capacity. Plan: adjust per-worker in-flight cap and apply soft-shedding on noisy routes. Preparing commands now.

sasha: Agreed. Recommend: set max_inflight_per_worker=32, soft_shed at 80% queue depth for /generate, reduce long-runner timeout to 18s. Also propose disabling the experimental /preview endpoint for free-tier for the next 45m — it's the biggest offender.

maya: Applying soft-shed + timeout change now. Command: ```sh
redwoodctl runtime set-route --route /generate --soft_shed_pct 80 --timeout 18s
```

ajay: Patching traffic-shaper config (rolling):
```yaml
# one-liner patch applied
kubectl patch cm traffic-shaper -n runtime --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_inflight_per_worker":"32"}}'
```
Rolling to one node at a time. Watching queue depth and token throughput.

sasha: Also enabling per-customer rate cap for free-tier to 30r/s to reduce noisy fanout. CLI: `redwoodctl quotas apply --tier free --rate 30`

tom: Customer impact check: preliminary numbers show ~6 tenants with 5-12% 500 spikes, mostly on BizApp and Playground. Support on standby to send brief customer notes if errors persist.

sasha: Telemetry update: 3m after soft-shed and rate limits, queue depth down ~40%, 95th latency trending down, error rate halved. Some clients still retry aggressively causing short tail.

maya: Rolling mitigation summary for handoff -> Applied: soft-shed 80% on /generate, timeout 18s, max_inflight_per_worker=32, free-tier rate cap 30r/s, disabled /preview for free-tier.

maya: Heads-up: I need to step out in ~30m. @liam can you take the active watch and escalate if we see reappearance? Notes: watch queue_depth, 95th latency, error-rate, and per-tenant retries.

liam: Ack — taking over. If spike returns, plan B: enable IP-based rate limiting and temporarily bump dedicated capacity for the busiest tenants. I'll also be ready to re-enable /preview after stability window.

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigations applied; severity downgraded to SEV3; created ticket INC-20260317. Timeline and commands logged.

maya: Leaving detailed postmortem skeleton in #incidents and will follow up with root cause once we have logs. For now leaving thread open for liam to close when stable. :white_check_mark:
